question: In a standard laser flash experiment, a thin porous sample of thickness $L = 4~\text{mm}$ and porosity $\phi = 0.5$ is saturated with static water. A short pulse of laser energy is shot at the front face ($x = 0$), and the temperature rise $\Delta T(t)$ is monitored at the back face ($x = L$). The half-rise time (the time it takes for the back face to reach half of its maximum temperature rise) is measured to be $t_{1/2} = 5.37~\text{s}$. The half-rise time can be described by Parker's classical relation ($t_{1/2} = 0.1388 \cdot \frac{L^2}{\alpha_{\text{eff}}}$). Assuming this holds, calculate the effective thermal conductivity ($k_{\text{eff}}$) in $\text{W/(m}\cdot\text{K)}$ under Local Thermal Equilibrium (LTE). Given properties: $\rho_f = 1000~\text{kg/m}^3$, $c_{pf} = 4200~\text{J/(kg}\cdot\text{K)}$, $\rho_s = 2500~\text{kg/m}^3$, $c_{ps} = 800~\text{J/(kg}\cdot\text{K)}$. Give your answer in $\text{W/(m}\cdot\text{K)}$ rounded to 2 decimal places.

answers.feedback: Correct! You found $\alpha_{\text{eff}} \approx 4.14 \times 10^{-7}~\text{m}^2/\text{s}$ and combined it with $(\rho c_p)_{\text{eff}} = 3.1 \times 10^6~\text{J/(m}^3\cdot\text{K)}$ to get $k_{\text{eff}} \approx 1.28~\text{W/(m}\cdot\text{K)}$.
